docs.title: SynOmicBench: A Unified Benchmark for Synthetic Cancer Omics
docs.text:
Welcome to the SynOmicBench documentation. This platform provides a comprehensive framework for the generation, evaluation, and benchmarking of synthetic clinical and transcriptomic data in the context of precision oncology.

Achieving an appropriate trade-off between biological utility and patient privacy remains a critical challenge for secure data sharing when applying high-dimensional omics datasets to artificial intelligence. SynOmicBench introduces the first disease-agnostic benchmarking study tailored to this domain, comparing state-of-the-art synthetic data generation (SDG) methods across multiple cancer types.

docs.title: 🔬 Framework Overview
docs.text:
Figure 1: Overview of the SynOmicBench benchmarking protocol. (a) Data sensitivity and high-dimensionality of clinical-transcriptomic profiles. (b) Case studies across three cancer types (ccRCC, Melanoma, NSCLC). (c) Standardized generation pipeline. (d) Multidimensional evaluation framework covering Broad Utility, Narrow Utility, and Privacy Risk.

The SynOmicBench pipeline combines standardized preprocessing with a multidimensional evaluation suite, prioritizing downstream biological validation alongside statistical fidelity and attack-based privacy assessment.

Key Findings

Our results indicate that no single method dominated all dimensions. However, Gaussian Copula achieved the most balanced performance across fidelity, utility, and privacy metrics. While synthetic data consistently reproduced signal directionality, it often exhibited attenuated effect sizes, supporting its primary use for hypothesis generation and model pre-training.

docs.title: 📊 Benchmarked Datasets
docs.text:
SynOmicBench utilizes three diverse cancer cohorts treated with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), reflecting realistic heterogeneity in sample size and transcriptomic dimensionality.

Dataset Patients Clinical Features Omics Features Expression Level Study Source ccRCC 311 52 40,934 TPM Braun et al. (2020) Melanoma 121 47 18,760 TPM Liu et al. (2019) NSCLC 152 14 21,969 TPM Ravi et al. (2023)

docs.title: 🤖 SDG Methods Evaluated
docs.text:
We benchmarked six configurations representing three major categories of synthetic data generation:

  1. Gaussian Copula: A statistical approach that models multivariate dependencies using copula functions.
  2. CTGAN: Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks, designed specifically for tabular data.
  3. TVAE: Tabular Variational Autoencoders, an adaptation of VAEs for mixed-type tabular datasets.
  4. Synthpop: A regression-based synthesis tool using sequential conditional distributions.
  5. Avatars (K5 & K10): A k-anonymity based approach that generates synthetic "avatars" from local patient neighborhoods.

docs.title: 📐 Evaluation Pillars
docs.text: SynOmicBench evaluates synthetic data through three primary lenses to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the utility-privacy trade-off:

docs.title: 1. Broad Utility (Statistical Fidelity)
docs.text: Validates the preservation of global statistical properties by comparing: * Univariate Similarity: Marginal distributions of individual attributes. * Bivariate Similarity: Inter-variable relationships and correlation structures.

docs.title: 2. Narrow Utility (Biological Signal)
docs.text: Evaluates task-specific performance in clinically relevant downstream analyses: * Differential Gene Expression (DGE): Preservation of fold-changes and p-values. * Gene Set Enrichment (GSEA/ssGSEA): Recovery of biological pathway activities. * Cell Deconvolution: Consistency in estimated immune cell fractions. * Survival Analysis: Preservation of Kaplan-Meier curves and Hazard Ratios. * Predictive Modeling: Transferability of classification models.

docs.title: 3. Privacy Risk
docs.text: Quantifies disclosure vulnerability aligned with EDPB regulatory principles: * Singling-Out: Risk of isolating a unique individual. * Linkability: Risk of connecting records from multiple datasets. * Inference: Risk of deducing sensitive attribute values.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: SynOmicBench provides comprehensive metrics for evaluating synthetic omics data across three dimensions:

docs.title: 1. Fidelity Metrics
docs.text: Measures how well synthetic data preserves statistical properties of the original data.

docs.title: Univariate Similarity
docs.text:
• File: metrics/fidelity/UnivariateSimilarity.py
  • Metrics: Distribution matching, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, Wasserstein distance

docs.title: Pairwise Similarity
docs.text:
• File: metrics/fidelity/PairwiseSimilarity.py
  • Metrics: Correlation preservation, pairwise distance matching

docs.title: Bayesian Comparison
docs.text:
• File: metrics/fidelity/BayesianComparison.py
  • Metrics: Bayesian estimation of similarity with uncertainty quantification

docs.title: Missing Value Similarity
docs.text:
• File: metrics/fidelity/MissingValueSimilarity.py
  • Metrics: Missing value pattern preservation

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text:
• File: metrics/fidelity/visualization.py
  • Features: Plotting utilities for fidelity comparison

docs.title: 2. Narrow Utility Metrics
docs.text: Evaluates utility for specific downstream analysis tasks.

docs.title: Differential Gene Expression (DGE)
docs.text:
• File: metrics/narrow_utility/DGE.py
  • Purpose: Assess if synthetic data preserves DGE patterns
  • Use case: Biomarker discovery analysis

docs.title: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)
docs.text:
• File: metrics/narrow_utility/GSEA.py
  • Purpose: Evaluate pathway-level preservation
  • Use case: Pathway analysis validation

docs.title: Survival Analysis
docs.text:
• File: metrics/narrow_utility/survival_analysis.py
  • Purpose: Test survival prediction utility
  • Use case: Clinical outcome prediction

docs.title: Predictive Modeling
docs.text:
• File: metrics/narrow_utility/predictive_model_comp.py
  • Purpose: Compare predictive power across datasets
  • Use case: Machine learning model training

docs.title: 3. Privacy Metrics
docs.text: Assesses re-identification risks in synthetic data.

  • FigurePrivacy/SinglingOutRisk_Uni.ipynb

  • FigurePrivacy/Linkabiliy.ipynb

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
from SynOmics.metrics.fidelity import UnivariateSimilarity, PairwiseSimilarity
from SynOmics.metrics.narrow_utility import DGE

# Calculate fidelity metrics
uni_sim = UnivariateSimilarity()
uni_score = uni_sim.compute(original_data, synthetic_data)

pair_sim = PairwiseSimilarity()
pair_score = pair_sim.compute(original_data, synthetic_data)

# Calculate narrow utility
dge = DGE()
dge_score = dge.compute(synthetic_data, ground_truth_pathways)

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text:
The library includes visualization tools for comparing results across multiple synthesis methods:

from SynOmics.metrics.fidelity.visualization import plot_comparison

plot_comparison(
    results_dict,
    metrics=['univariate', 'pairwise', 'bayesian'],
    output_dir='figures/'
)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from SynOmics.processing import Preprocess, Pipeline

# Initialize preprocessing
preprocessor = Preprocess()
cleaned_data = preprocessor.normalize(raw_data)

# Use pipeline for full workflow
pipeline = Pipeline(synthesizer='gaussian_copula')
synthetic_data = pipeline.fit_transform(original_data)

docs.title: Synthesizers
docs.text: The SynOmics library provides multiple data synthesis methods for omics data.

docs.title: 1. Gaussian Copula Synthesizer
docs.text:
• File: synthesizer/GaussianCopulasynthesizer.py
  • Description: Uses Gaussian copula for flexible multivariate dependency modeling
  • Best for: Continuous data with complex correlations

docs.title: 2. CTGAN Synthesizer
docs.text:
• File: synthesizer/CTGANsynthesizer.py
  • Description: Conditional Tabular GAN for synthetic data generation
  • Best for: Mixed data types (continuous + categorical)

docs.title: 3. TVAE Synthesizer
docs.text:
• File: synthesizer/TVAEsynthesizer.py
  • Description: Tabular Variational Autoencoder
  • Best for: High-dimensional tabular data

docs.title: 4. MICE Synthesizer
docs.text:
• File: synthesizer/MICEsynthesizer.py
  • Description: Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations
  • Best for: Data with missing values

docs.title: 5. SynthPop Synthesizer
docs.text:
• File: synthesizer/Synthpopsynthesizer.py
  • Description: SynthPop method adapted for omics data
  • Best for: Preserving utility for downstream analysis

docs.title: 6. Gaussian Multivariate
docs.text:
• File: synthesizer/GaussianMultivariate_Parallel.py
  • Description: Multivariate Gaussian distribution modeling
  • Best for: Fast synthesis with correlation preservation

docs.title: Base Class
docs.text:
All synthesizers inherit from BaseSynthesizer:

from SynOmics.synthesizer import BaseSynthesizer

class BaseSynthesizer:
    def fit(self, data):
        """Fit the synthesizer to the data"""
        pass

    def sample(self, n_samples):
        """Generate synthetic samples"""
        pass

    def save(self, path):
        """Save the model"""
        pass

    def load(self, path):
        """Load the model"""
        pass

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
from SynOmics.synthesizer import GaussianCopulasynthesizer
import pandas as pd

# Load your omics data
data = pd.read_csv('your_omics_data.csv')

# Initialize and fit the synthesizer
synth = GaussianCopulasynthesizer()
synth.fit(data)

# Generate synthetic data
synthetic_data = synth.sample(n_samples=1000)

# Save the model
synth.save('model.pkl')
